races.title: State House, District 32
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Frank Sossamon
cands.bio: Republican and longtime pastor from Henderson area. Senior pastor of South Henderson Pentecostal Holiness Church for 36 years. Served in the North Carolina House for District 32 (Vance and most of Granville counties) from 2023 to 2025. Lost re-election in 2024 to Bryan Cohn.
cands.gaps: We could not find his exact birthplace, where he grew up, or when he settled in the district beyond his campaign's statement of 40 years. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or growth limits, and none on homestead property taxes. We also found no abortion, gun or immigration positions, and nothing on police pay or pensions. The sponsored-bills list on his Ballotpedia page was empty, so we could not confirm which bills he sponsored beyond his own claim of House Bill 982. His campaign site describes his votes (school choice, Medicaid expansion, the Parents Bill of Rights, the Farm Act, women's sports), but we could not confirm them from official records. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 55: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as North Carolina and his campaign site calls him a North Carolina native who has lived in District 32 for 40 years, but where he grew up is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: One term in the NC House (2023-2025), serving on the Appropriations and Commerce committees among others; 36 years as senior pastor of a church; president and board member of several Crime Stoppers and juvenile crime prevention groups.
qual.why: Prior legislative service puts him above the middle band, but there is only one term and no law, policy or budget career. His church leadership is counted as management experience. Committee seats and nonprofit boards add nothing.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he voted for the "Choose Your School, Choose Your Future" bill expanding Opportunity Scholarships. This is his own claim; no roll call was available to confirm it.

land-for-floridians.evidence: His campaign site says he is committed to reclaiming farmland held by foreign adversaries and to preventing commercial interests from monopolizing agricultural land.

cands.name: Bryan K. Cohn
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 32 (Granville and Vance counties) since January 2025. Works in agriculture and owns a small business in Oxford. Married father of three.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from Sway voting groups, including NC Public School Champions, Fair Map Fight Club, Better Future NC, Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Elizabeth's Picks, Imani's Pix and Unburdening The Ballot.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Bryan Cohn was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. His specific work history in agriculture and his business's name and details are not documented in the pages we read. His campaign site refers to becoming a public servant in 2021, and we could not find what role that was. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, guns, or campaign-money pledges. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read, so we could not confirm any specific legislative action. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. The campaign site's claim that he fought to protect local control of public water resources is not backed by a record we could open.
